target.transport: native USB composite CDC and HID mouse, plus authenticated Wi-Fi OTA when ignored credentials are present
target.current_device_policy: Before flashing a StickS3 used by another project, identify its serial port and preserve the complete flash under ignored .device-backups. The tested unit has a verified recovery image. OTA must resolve sticks3-ptt.local and match the saved AC:27:6E:D2:68:B8 hardware MAC; bedside-countdown-s3 is a separate device and must never be targeted.

validated_facts.fact: The internal IMU is a BMI270 at I2C address 0x68 on SDA GPIO47 and SCL GPIO48.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack StickS3 documentation and M5Unified StickS3 board implementation

validated_facts.fact: The internal infrared transmitter is GPIO46 and the infrared receiver is GPIO42.
The infrared receiver is a demodulating digital receiver intended for RMT pulse capture, not an analog reflectance channel.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack documents RMT-only reception and its remote-control distance guidance; this makes blink sensing unproven until measured.

validated_facts.fact: The internal IR path needs the controlled external 5 V output and must not be enabled while an external source drives that rail.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack StickS3 power and IR documentation; firmware defaults the rail off and requires a physical two-second hold.

validated_facts.fact: USB HID on ESP32-S3 requires TinyUSB native mode ARDUINO_USB_MODE=0; ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1 selects hardware USB-JTAG CDC and cannot run USBHIDMouse.
validated_facts.validation: Espressif Arduino core 2.0.17 and 3.x USB examples, installed core sources, and Context7 official-source excerpts

validated_facts.fact: Wokwi can execute a generic ESP32-S3 DevKitC firmware image, but its documented board list does not provide a complete StickS3 model.
validated_facts.validation: Official Wokwi ESP32 guide, Wokwi CLI documentation, Context7 Wokwi documentation index, and a successful Wokwi CLI run of the cross-compiled simulator harness

validated_facts.fact: No public tool currently provides a complete StickS3 emulator.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack lv_m5_emulator is a native SDL UI tool whose current targets omit StickS3; UiFlow2 runs programs on a connected device; Espressif QEMU covers the ESP32-S3 SoC only; Wokwi exposes a generic ESP32-S3 rather than the complete board.

validated_facts.fact: The tested StickS3 enumerates as a native TinyUSB composite CDC and HID mouse, initializes its BMI270, accepts the large blue Button A, and moves the host pointer from head motion while mounted on glasses.
validated_facts.validation: Physical 2026-08-14 bench and worn-device tests; a stationary armed control produced zero host input events before the worn pointer test.

validated_facts.fact: The integrated IR pair is not a viable near-eye reflectance sensor in the tested geometry.
validated_facts.validation: Multiple physical tests produced inseparable or malformed near-eye data; M5Stack specifies direct TX/RX alignment at no less than 30 cm and warns that shorter spacing causes abnormal reception.

validated_facts.fact: Firm blinks transfer measurable sub-degree-per-second impulses through a rigid glasses mount to the BMI270, but evenly spaced blink counting is unsafe.
validated_facts.validation: Five new worn guided runs produced three still-control sequences and only two intentional sequences with the former four-blink cadence. A fixed-threshold search could remove controls only by losing intended runs. The replacement 1.1 dps double-pause-double pattern replays every retained still/head control with zero sequences but still needs a new worn validation.

validated_facts.fact: The tested StickS3's original PTT project supports authenticated ArduinoOTA as sticks3-ptt.local, while bedside-countdown-s3 is a separate LilyGO T-Display-S3.
validated_facts.validation: Read-only inspection of the original PTT build script and firmware, live mDNS discovery of the separate bedside board, and saved hardware identities. Colibrino now preserves the PTT OTA credentials and hostname behind ignored configuration and a MAC-guarded uploader.

validated_facts.fact: StickS3 contains the microphone, ES8311 codec, speaker path, 8 MB PSRAM, and ESP32-S3 resources needed for a local wake-word proof.
validated_facts.validation: M5Stack hardware documentation, the official StickS3 Xiaozhi firmware guide, and the open Xiaozhi StickS3 board definition. This proves the audio chain, not Colibrino voice accuracy or safety.

validated_facts.fact: ESP-SR supports ESP32-S3 local WakeNet and MultiNet recognition, but current MultiNet command models do not support Portuguese.
validated_facts.validation: Espressif ESP-SR WakeNet, MultiNet, AFE, model-loading, and benchmark documentation checked directly and through Context7.

validated_facts.fact: The validated Colibrino toolchain and flash layout cannot accept the current Arduino ESP_SR path without deliberate migration work.
validated_facts.validation: PlatformIO resolves Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17 while the current Arduino ESP_SR wrapper belongs to 3.x; the installed 8 MB layout has dual OTA slots and no speech-model partition.

validated_facts.fact: ESP32-S3 can provide BLE HID but not Bluetooth LE Audio.
validated_facts.validation: Espressif ESP32-S3 Bluetooth capability documentation. The intended near-term voice path is local recognition, not using StickS3 as a standard Bluetooth microphone.

validated_facts.fact: A bulky TCRT5000 module is not the only external blink-sensor option.
validated_facts.validation: Vishay documents a 2.0 by 1.0 by 0.5 mm VCNL36828P proximity device for smart-glasses applications; ST documents the compact VL53L4CD up to 100 Hz with a Class 1 940 nm emitter. Neither is validated on this user or mount.

validated_facts.fact: Arduino Nicla Voice is a credible lower-power second prototype, not a selected replacement.
validated_facts.validation: Arduino documents a 22.86 mm, approximately 2 g board with NDP120, nRF52832 BLE, BMI270, microphone, 16 MB flash, and battery support; its factory Alexa demo measurements are 0.8 mA BLE-off and 2.4 mA with advertising plus one-hertz sensor polling. BLE HID and high-rate multimodal use remain unproven.

tasks.name: Separate StickS3 target
acceptance: Legacy AVR source remains untouched.
StickS3 has its own pinned PlatformIO environment.
A native host-test environment compiles sensor-independent logic.

tasks.name: Safe USB head-mouse prototype
acceptance: BMI270 data calibrates only while stationary.
Movement uses gyro rate with filtering, deadzone, fractional accumulation, and bounded HID reports.
The device emits no pointer movement until mouse mode is physically armed for two seconds.
Axis directions are verified on the glasses mount and head motion moves the host pointer.
A stationary armed control produces no spontaneous HID movement.

tasks.name: Onboard IR blink feasibility probe
acceptance: Transmit GPIO46 emits a controlled 38 kHz carrier envelope through RMT.
Receive GPIO42 captures raw demodulated pulse timing through RMT.
CDC logs retain timestamp, validity, symbol count, active time, total time, normalized ratio, and protocol stage.
The guided test measures open eye, closed eye, and repeated blinks without assuming signal polarity.
A pass requires at least 20 valid frames in each baseline, at least 4 sigma separation, at least 15 percent relative change, and at least two human-duration blink events.
Physical near-eye failure is retained as evidence and does not get relabeled as a capability.

tasks.name: External click-sensor boundary
acceptance: Blink classification consumes a sensor-neutral normalized sample.
A future analog TCRT5000 implementation can replace the onboard IR producer without changing USB click behavior.
No TCRT5000 purchase is recommended until the coded IMU pattern receives one focused worn validation run.

tasks.name: StickS3 bench validation
acceptance: Firmware build completes without flashing as the pre-hardware gate.
StickS3 enumerates as both CDC and HID without spontaneous mouse reports.
Display reports BMI270 and stationary calibration succeeds.
Worn-device head motion moves the pointer with the expected axes.
High-rate stillness, deliberate-blink, and ordinary-head-motion CSV is retained outside Git.
The double-pause-double IMU pattern passes twice and produces zero still/head control-stage events in a fresh run.

tasks.name: Generic ESP32-S3 simulator gate
acceptance: The portable production motion, optical blink-analysis, and IMU pattern sources cross-compile for a generic ESP32-S3 target.
Wokwi CLI lints the diagram and boots the firmware image.

The simulated firmware validates stationary gyro calibration, moving-calibration rejection, cursor deadzone, pointer direction and accumulation, invalid timestep rejection, optical separation, blink timing, the double-pause-double IMU pattern, uniform-blink rejection, head-motion cancellation, and the complete guided feasibility protocol.
The run emits COLIBRINO_SIM_PASS and does not claim to validate unmodeled StickS3 peripherals or optics.

tasks.name: IMU-only blink gesture
acceptance: One through three temple impulses never recommend a click.
Four bounded impulses are required as two 300-700 millisecond double-blink gaps separated by one 800-1400 millisecond deliberate pause.
Uniformly spaced four-blink cadence never recommends a click.
Pointer-scale rotation cancels partial state and suppresses detection for two quiet seconds.
A guided run records zero patterns during ordinary blinking, at least two during deliberate double-pause-double groups, and zero during head movement.
Runtime HID clicking remains disabled unless the complete current-boot guided run passes.

tasks.name: Authenticated StickS3 OTA
acceptance: Wi-Fi and ArduinoOTA compile only when the ignored device secrets header is available.
The service reuses the tested unit's established sticks3-ptt.local identity and authenticated password.
OTA start locks HID, releases mouse buttons, invalidates blink validation, cancels capture, and disables external 5 V before transfer.
The upload wrapper refuses any resolved device whose ARP MAC differs from AC:27:6E:D2:68:B8.
One cable flash installed the listener on the explicitly matched AC:27:6E:D2:68:B8 ROM download port.

After bootstrap, two authenticated OTA round trips succeeded; each reboot returned with HID locked, IR off, BMI270 calibrated, blink clicks disabled, and OTA ready while bedside-countdown-s3 remained untouched.
A third authenticated OTA upload installed the double-pause-double build before USB was disconnected; post-reboot CDC confirmation remains pending.

tasks.name: Isolated StickS3 wake-word proof
acceptance: A separate Arduino-ESP32 3.x or ESP-IDF environment preserves the validated production environment.
A measured partition plan fits the application and selected models and documents how OTA and recovery remain viable.
The ES8311 microphone feeds continuous 16 kHz mono audio to a built-in WakeNet phrase and six to ten offline commands.
The proof emits diagnostics and display state only; it cannot emit HID.
Quiet, soft, television, conversation, fan, glasses-rub, seated, and lying tests retain false-wake, rejection, latency, and power evidence.

tasks.name: Multimodal intent and BLE architecture
acceptance: IMU, voice, blink, dwell, and external-switch producers emit bounded AccessIntent values rather than transport side effects.
One application safety reducer owns click, drag, release, recenter, pause, confidence, cooldown, and arming policy.
A wake phrase freezes pointer output before a short command window; a bare command word never clicks.
USB and BLE transport loss, host sleep, pairing loss, reboot, low battery, and task failure release all buttons and discard stale intent.
Wi-Fi remains off in normal wearable operation and authenticated OTA requires explicit maintenance mode.

tasks.name: Apple and alternate-hardware comparison
acceptance: The intended user's actual speech or reliable sounds are compared with macOS Vocal Shortcuts and Voice Control before custom model training.
Switch Control, Dwell, Head Pointer, and Live Speech integration are checked with standard HID or switch semantics.
If IMU blink fails, a compact documented near-eye sensor is evaluated before a bulky TCRT5000 module.
StickS3 and Nicla Voice are compared using the same motion latency, wake accuracy, negative-audio soak, battery, weight, pairing, and recovery protocol.
No final board or sensor purchase decision is made without physical evidence.

simulation_boundary.validated_in_wokwi: ESP32-S3 compilation and execution of sensor-independent motion, statistics, optical blink detection, coded double-pause-double IMU detection, uniform-blink rejection, cancellation gates, and feasibility state-machine logic.
simulation_boundary.requires_sticks3_hardware: Regression of BMI270 mounting behavior, M5PM1 power control, display, buttons, composite TinyUSB CDC/HID, the IMU gesture across users and remounts, and any external click sensor.

available_tools.not_covered: Complete StickS3 board, onboard IR optics, and exact composite USB behavior

sensor_purchase_decision.onboard_ir_pass: Do not use the integrated demodulating IR pair as a near-eye click sensor; its documented spacing and physical results reject that geometry.
sensor_purchase_decision.imu_retest: Repeat the guided double-pause-double run on the final rigid mount. Keep it only if at least two intentional patterns and zero ordinary-blink or head-motion patterns are recorded in repeated sessions.
sensor_purchase_decision.external_sensor_required: When the IMU gesture cannot pass consistently, is too tiring, or produces any control-stage event, evaluate a compact sensor with a documented near-eye safety case such as a VL53L4CD-class ToF part before choosing a bulky TCRT5000 module. Every option still needs a schematic, optical review, and physical mount test.

remaining_hardware_questions: Does the double-pause-double BMI270 gesture pass after repeated removal and remounting of the glasses?
Is a coded four-blink click usable enough for the intended user, or only a proof that no external sensor is electrically required?
If an external sensor is needed, does a compact Class 1 ToF or reviewed proximity part detect the eyelid reliably at a safe glasses geometry?
When should the preserved original flash image be restored to the tested StickS3 after the remaining hardware run?
Can the intended user reliably produce a wake phrase, command, or consistent non-word sound while seated and lying down, and is Portuguese required?
Can an actual WakeNet plus command build retain dual OTA in 8 MB, and what one-time cable partition migration is required?
Does continuous audio plus high-rate BMI270 sampling preserve pointer timing and useful battery runtime?
Can Nicla Voice provide robust BLE HID, high-rate motion, personalized audio inference, and fail-closed reconnect behavior?
